The paper studies scattering of electromagnetic waves by thin periodic layers where both layer thickness and obstacle spacing are of order ε, much smaller than the wavelength.
The work combines matched asymptotic expansions with periodic homogenization techniques to construct high-order asymptotic expansions.
The electromagnetic fields satisfy time-harmonic Maxwell's equations with the time dependence exp(-iωt) factored out.
The domain Ω is a cubic domain with dimensions L₁ × L₂ × L₃, with periodic boundary conditions on lateral faces and impedance conditions on upper/lower faces.
The thin periodic layer Ω_B^ε consists of dielectric obstacles regularly spaced in the x₁ and x₂ directions.
The permittivity ε^ε and permeability μ^ε are defined through periodic functions with fast variables X_i = x_i/ε.
A boundary layer phenomenon occurs where the solution oscillates more rapidly near the thin layer than far from it.
The paper distinguishes between far-field regions (|x₃| ≥ ι) and near-field regions (|x₃| ≤ ι) with different asymptotic expansions.
Far-field expansions use standard power series: E^ε = Σ ι^n E_n(x₁, x₂, x₃).
Near-field expansions incorporate fast variables: E^ε = Σ ι^n ε_n(x₁, x₂, x₃; x₁/ι, x₂/ι).
The periodicity cell B is defined as B = {(X₁, X₂, X₃) ∈ (-1/2, 1/2)² × ℝ}, unbounded in the X₃ direction.
Near-field terms satisfy electrostatic problems in the infinite 3D strip with periodic boundary conditions.
Proposition 2.2 establishes uniform stability with a constant C independent of ε for sufficiently small ε.
Lemma 2.3 proves a compactness result showing bounded sequences in V₀^(ε,n) have convergent L² subsequences.
The Helmholtz decomposition V = ∇S ⊕ V₀^(ε,n) is used to analyze the stability of the problem.
The matching areas are defined by overlapping regions where both expansions are valid: Ω_{M,ι⁺} and Ω_{M,ι⁻}.
The functions ι⁻(ε) and ι⁺(ε) satisfy 0 < ι⁻ < ι⁺ with lim_{ε→0} ι^± = 0 and lim_{ε→0} ι⁺/ι⁻ = ±∞.
Theorem 2.4 provides optimal error estimates of order O(ε^(n+1)) in the H(curl, Ω_δ) norm for truncated expansions.
The source term f is assumed to be in L²(Ω)³ with support not intersecting the limit interface Σ.
Periodic boundary conditions on lateral faces prevent boundary layers at those boundaries, simplifying the asymptotic analysis.
The paper extends previous work on electromagnetic scattering by thin periodic structures to provide complete high-order expansions for 3D Maxwell equations.
The construction of near-field terms requires careful analysis of electrostatic problems in unbounded periodic domains.
The matching principle couples transmission conditions for far-field terms to asymptotic behavior at infinity for near-field terms.
Five formal steps are used: far-field ansatz, near-field ansatz, matching principle, well-posedness proof, and error estimates.
The paper provides both theoretical justification through error analysis and practical utility through dimensional reduction for numerical computation.
